title: Personal Hygiene
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Keep this sub-strand kind: never point at a child's own body, clothes or smell. Use a tippy-tap made from a jerrycan so the class can wash hands with running water.

skills.key_step: The child names practices that keep the body clean and healthy (bathing daily, brushing teeth twice a day, washing hands, cutting nails, combing hair, wearing clean clothes) and says why each matters.

floor.prerequisite: Knows materials used to clean the body.
floor.question: What do we use to clean our teeth?

representations: a picture chart of a daily routine
a toothbrush, comb, soap and nail cutter
steps: Say what it protects us from.

misconceptions.repair: Ask whether perfume washes dirt and germs off the skin.

misconceptions.ask: How often should teeth be brushed?
misconceptions.repair: Look at how quickly a smooth tooth feels rough again.

listen_for: Hands that look clean cannot have germs
misconceptions.ask: Why must hands that look clean still be washed before eating?
misconceptions.repair: Rub clean-looking hands in glitter or powder and see how it spreads.

listen_for: They do not matter if hands are washed
misconceptions.ask: Why should nails be kept short and clean?
misconceptions.repair: Use a toothpick (gently) to show the dirt under a long nail after gardening.

checks.question: How often should you brush your teeth?
Why should we bathe daily?
checks.answer: to remove sweat, dirt and germs

skills.key_step: The child says when to wash hands (before eating and cooking, after the toilet, after handling animals or rubbish) and how (running water, soap, rub all parts including between the fingers and under the nails for about 20 seconds, rinse, dry on a clean towel or in the air).
representations: glitter on hands to stand for germs
steps: Wet the hands with running water.
Soap all parts: palms, backs, between fingers, nails.
Rub while you count to twenty.
Rinse and dry on a clean towel or in the air.

board.do: Draw two hands with dots for germs between the fingers.
Ask whether a quick rinse with no soap will remove them.
Rub with soap on the drawing and wipe the dots away.

misconceptions.ask: What do we use to wash hands properly?
misconceptions.repair: Wash greasy hands with water only and then with soap.

listen_for: One second, a quick dip is enough
misconceptions.ask: How long should hands be rubbed with soap?
misconceptions.repair: Count while rubbing with soap and talk about how long it takes to reach under the nails.
Ask what is on hands before a meal after playing outside.

misconceptions.ask: How should you dry your hands after washing?
misconceptions.repair: Ask where the germs on the dirty shirt go when wet hands touch it.

checks.question: Name two times you must wash your hands.
checks.answer: any two of before eating, after the toilet, after touching animals

checks.question: What do you use with water to wash hands well?
